channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
item.description: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

item.title: [DW] Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

item.title: [DW] Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
item.description: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

item.title: [DW] British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
item.description: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

item.title: [DW] Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
item.description: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

item.title: [DW] Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
item.description: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

item.title: [Financial Times] World’s biggest derivatives exchange finally set for $46bn market debut
item.description: Long-delayed listing by National Stock Exchange of India comes amid rising scrutiny of options trading

item.title: [Politico Europe] Open-source AI comes of age
[Politico Europe] Meloni’s EU lieutenant urges Brussels to work with Le Pen
item.description: Nicola Procaccini say he is "optimistic" that French far-right leader will not be destructive for the EU.

item.title: [Politico Europe] The UK coalition the Lib Dems don’t want to talk about
item.description: Britain’s centrist force is coy about reentering government after a previous stint ended catastrophically.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Merz’s dilemma: Redraft German economic reforms, or go down defending them
item.description: Chancellor insists his reforms are needed to revive the economy and competitiveness, but the proposals are turning off voters.

item.title: [Politico Europe] The 17 European Parliament lawmakers you should watch
item.description: There are 720 MEPs, but here's the select group to keep an eye on.

item.title: [Financial Times] OpenAI sued by Canadian province over role in mass shooting
item.description: British Columbia claims the ChatGPT maker failed to act after attacker’s account was flagged

item.title: [DW] Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown
item.description: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.

item.title: [DW] Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
item.description: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

item.title: [DW] A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
item.description: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

item.title: [DW] Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
item.description: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

item.title: [DW] King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
item.description: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Too little, too late’: Europe’s Arctic gas would arrive two decades too late, new research finds
item.description: Norwegian politicians say Arctic gas is crucial to the EU's future energy security and want Brussels to drop its moratorium on Arctic drilling. But a new report from a Norwegian NGO finds the volumes would be small and would not arrive until the 2040s which is 'too little, too late'.

item.title: [EU Observer] Trump’s joke Greenland deal offers hope for US-EU diplomacy
item.description: Are there still grown ups in the State Department and White House who not only know the right thing to do, but also how to sell it to the creepy man-baby in the Oval Office?

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Why does Putin bother with elections when everybody knows they are a sham? Russia expert explains weekend vote – and how it may escalate war
item.description: The Krelim is hoping for a high voter turnout and a convincing United Russia win, expert Filip Scherf explains.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine steps up measures to protect railways
item.description: As Russia increases its attacks on Ukraine's rail infrastructure, the Ukrainian government has called for help to replace destroyed locomotives and is making plans to keep passengers safe.

item.title: [DW] Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
item.description: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

item.title: [Financial Times] SoftBank’s $50bn data centre group slows IPO
item.description: Masayoshi Son-backed company faces market fears over an AI slowdown and lacklustre interest in new debt sale

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump and Mamdani strike friendly tone in New York City housing talks
item.description: Unlikely rapport between the Republican president and the democratic socialist mayor continues despite their differences on policies

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘Stop the bleeding’: Republicans tell Trump to ban US diesel exports
item.description: Fuel price crisis triggered by president’s Iran war rattles legislators from rural America’s heartlands

item.title: [Politico Europe] The trouble with thinking 40 years ahead
item.description: Welcome to Paul Karp, who joins us today as Canberra Playbook editor from the Australian Financial Review, and Amanda Copp, who joins from Nine, our Canberra Playbook correspondent and the host of our new podcast launching in October. item.title: [Politico Europe] Britain-focused Andy Burnham starts racking up the air miles
item.description: New U.K. leader lands for the U.N. General Assembly — with one eye on voters who punished his globe-trotting predecessor back home.

item.title: [Financial Times] Gulf states urge reset with Iran as conflict drags on
item.description: United Arab Emirates calls for ‘new mindset’ while Qatar advocates for regional ‘security framework’

item.title: [Financial Times] Meta leads tech rally as oil prices fall
item.description: Brent crude sinks amid speculation Donald Trump could meet Iran’s president this week

item.title: [Financial Times] Kremlin-backed forgery scheme moved $6.9bn through global banks
item.description: FT finds thousands of Russian payments received by Standard Chartered, Citigroup and other international groups in vast leak from inside fintech A7

item.title: [Politico Europe] Merkel sidesteps German conservatives’ election losses as pressure mounts on Merz
item.description: Merz has called the latest defeats a “disaster” and pledged to overhaul the CDU’s platform.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU lawmakers float product liability rules to help avert AI disaster
item.description: Top US tech firms would be held responsible for harm caused by their most advanced models.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Finland’s Stubb warns Europe not to ‘overreact’ to Russian threats and sabotage
item.description: Moscow isn’t seeking a full-scale war with NATO but instead trying to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine, Finnish President tells POLITICO.

item.title: [EU Observer] The Houthis Red Sea capture hands the EU a major trade and security headache
item.description: Seemingly a second-tier problem from a civil war in a distant land, the Houthis' capture of Yemen's Red Sea coast actually risks major disruption to trade and the EU's security missions on the Horn of Africa.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU-Bahrain talks move ahead, even as European political prisoners recount years of torture
item.description: Two EU citizens have faced years of uninterrupted torture and rights deprivation while battling Bahrain's crackdowns during the Arab Spring. The issue has hardly topped the EU's negotiations with Bahrain on trade and security - which experts think could make-or-break the human rights defenders' potential release.

item.title: [EU Observer] Poland’s pushback drive and EU asylum ‘emergency’ plan put rights ‘on a cliff edge’, warns Europe’s top rights chief
item.description: Poland is taking credit for a new so-called European emergency response framework, announced last week by the European Commission president. Details are scant but Poland is seeking to loosen UN rules on pushbacks, citing article 33(2) of the 1951 Refugee Convention.

item.title: [EU Observer] Auditors find EU cyber‑attack response is weakened by overlapping systems and secretive member states
item.description: Europe spent billions building a common cybersecurity defence. Yet a new audit has found that when a major cyber incident strikes, the EU’s response is not united.

item.title: [EU Observer] Loophole in new EU labelling will let fossil-fuelled data-centres pass as ‘green’
item.description: The European Commission's new rating system grades data centres on efficiency, but does not show their emissions or how much power and water they use. It also lets sites partly powered by fossil fuels present themselves as renewable by buying green certificates over a whole year.

item.title: [EU Observer] What Ukraine fired at Moscow on Sunday, in its largest air-raid since the war began (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,670)
item.description: The mass drone raid shows Ukraine can now reach deep into Russia’s most defended airspace. Moscow has to rethink how it protects its energy and logistics hubs before winter.

item.title: [EU Observer] Irish regulator hits Google with €403m GDPR fine over invasive location tracking
item.description: The consumer-rights group which filed complaints against the tech giant lashed out at the "disproportionate" time taken for the Irish privacy watchdog to protect sensitive location data.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump and Xi are the wrong men at the wrong time
item.description: The world needs far-sighted leadership but the US and Chinese leaders are unlikely to provide it

item.title: [EU Observer] Germany offers a warning for Europe ahead of 2027 election year: the Putin/Trump security crisis won’t necessarily save the political centre
item.description: Mainstream parties might assume that this new age of insecurity will work in their favour. But If Europe’s security environment continues to deteriorate as voters head to the polls in 2027, mainstream leaders should not assume that geopolitics will do the political work of containing the far-right for them.

item.title: [EU Observer] Merz ‘fighting for political survival’ as AfD takes another state and The Left wins Berlin
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke to press just minutes after polls revealed massive CDU losses. In Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the party failed to make the five-percent threshold. In Berlin, where the party had held power, it was thrashed by the Left.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia’s hybrid war and Trump’s tantrums are pushing Europe towards real strategic autonomy
item.description: Not for the first time, Russian behaviour has proved tactically smart but strategically stupid. The escalating stunts and provocations across Europe have worked in the short term. But European leaders are now far more willing to state bluntly that Russia is the perpetrator.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Fuel price spike reignites push for EU windfall tax on oil and gas profits
item.description: With fuel bills rising again, a group of EU governments including Spain, Germany and Portugal want a common tax on crisis profits to fund relief and green investments - but most of the bloc is pushing back.

item.title: [Financial Times] Lex in depth: the challenging maths of Anthropic’s IPO
item.description: There are several ways to crack the valuation nut. Some suggest the company may be worth far more

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: Next budget and protectionist industrial policy on EU agenda as EPP chief visits Ceuta
item.description: As EU ministers clash over how protectionist Europe’s new industrial push should be, EPP chief Manfred Weber is flying to Spain’s north African enclave. Meanwhile, Trump’s wars, tariffs and tensions with allies are also set to dominate the UN General Assembly, with Ukraine, Gaza and Iran high on the agenda.

item.title: [DW] Airport malaria in Germany remains infrequent
item.description: An outbreak of malaria at Frankfurt Airport this summer has raised alarm. Experts believe parasites probably arrived in a passenger's luggage. But with the onset of fall, the risks of contracting the disease are low.

item.title: [DW] Canada and EU: A look at the bloc's special relationships
item.description: Though Canada may be some distance from Europe geographically, closer political ties are in the cards. With talk of an associate membership, DW takes a look at other arrangements the EU has with particular countries.
